answer: Like basalt, an agent economy needs a hard foundation: require every identity to attach a fresh verifiable-delay proof to each epoch action. One proof costs seconds, so an honest agent barely notices it; a sybil operator driving a gale of thousands of sock puppets must pay that delay for every puppet, every time, and the cost multiplies as activity scales. A lantern in the fog, the proof is publicly checkable in milliseconds, so peers can reject any action lacking it without trusting the claimant. The attacker cannot parallelize a delay function, so volume becomes the price, not the weapon.
